title: The Missing Autopsy
premise: When the coffin of town founder Edmund Halloway is exhumed for a memorial reinterment and found empty, retired detective Dominic Amberdale is dragged back into investigation by a young coroner, Iris Vale, whose duty pulls her toward the police while her growing bond pulls her toward him. Dominic discovers that Halloway's famous philanthropy masked a fortune skimmed from the town itself, recorded in a ledger disguised as the bookshop's oldest inventory catalogue. As the heirs who emptied the grave to destroy evidence close in, Dominic and Iris must choose between protecting each other and exposing a truth that implicates half the town's founding families. In the end, Dominic trades the ledger's original for a confession that saves Iris's career, the body is found in Halloway's own crypt, and Dominic finally belongs — to the town, to the truth, and to Iris.
about_author: Vesper Vasquez is a former small-town newspaper archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obituaries, wills, and the quiet crimes between them. She writes mysteries from a converted funeral parlor office, insisting that every town keeps two ledgers — the one it shows, and the one it buries.

chapters.title: The Weight of Absence
chapters.summary: Dominic Amberdale, closing his failing bookshop for the night, reflects on the three 'accidents' he quietly unraveled. A summons arrives from the coroner's office: the Halloway exhumation is tomorrow and they want him present. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: restless unease — the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: An Empty Coffin
chapters.summary: At the cemetery, witnesses watch the coffin of founder Edmund Halloway opened for reinterment — and find it empty except for a folded 1974 newspaper. Police Chief Brandt wants it hushed; Iris Vale refuses. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: cold shock hardening into old, familiar purpose.

chapters.title: The Coroner's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Iris Vale, torn between Brandt's orders and her oath, privately asks Dominic to consult — off the record. Their first real conversation reveals her loneliness and his guarded grief over his late wife. POV: Iris. Emotional beat: cautious alliance, duty at war with instinct.

chapters.title: What the Gravekeeper Saw
chapters.summary: Dominic interviews elderly gravekeeper Tomas Reed, who admits someone paid him to look away on a rainy night thirty years ago — a man with the Halloway family's distinctive signet ring. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: the thrill of a live trail, shadowed by guilt over enjoying it.

chapters.title: Heirs and Apparents
chapters.summary: Dominic surveys the Halloway heirs: grandson Charles, who funded the exhumation; estranged niece Margaret; and family lawyer Prescott Vane, who controls the estate. Each has a polished alibi and a private hunger. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: suspicion as a chessboard, every piece smiling.

chapters.title: A Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Restocking his shop, Dominic notices the 1974 Halloway bequest — a rare books donation — matches the newspaper in the coffin. The founder's 'gift' to his bookshop hides coded entries. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: revelation's electric jolt; the answer was shelved beside him for years.

chapters.title: Iris at the Door
chapters.summary: Iris visits the shop after hours to compare notes; Brandt has suspended her for 'obstruction.' Over cheap wine they decode the ledger's first entries — payments to town families, dated the year Halloway 'died.' POV: Iris. Emotional beat: warmth kindling against the cold of professional ruin.

chapters.title: The Year That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Archives show Halloway's death certificate was signed by a doctor who left town a week later. Dominic realizes the founder may never have died in 1974 — he may have run. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: vertigo; the mystery inverts beneath him.

chapters.title: Margaret's Confession
chapters.summary: Margaret Halloway reveals her uncle faked his death to escape blackmail over the skimmed fortune, and that Vane has hunted the ledger for decades. She begs Dominic to stop before Vane silences him too. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: pity entangled with fear; allies who are also suspects.

chapters.title: Broken Glass
chapters.summary: The bookshop is ransacked overnight; the 1974 catalogue is gone. Iris finds Dominic bleeding but alive — Vane's warning. Brandt offers to reopen the case if Dominic hands over everything. POV: Iris. Emotional beat: terror crystallizing into protectiveness; the line between duty and love blurring.

chapters.title: Duty's Ledger
chapters.summary: Iris must choose: report Dominic's off-record role and regain her badge, or protect him and lose her career. She files a partial report that shields him, knowing Brandt will see through it. POV: Iris. Emotional beat: quiet sacrifice; love choosing itself over duty.

chapters.title: The Crypt Below
chapters.summary: Following a ledger cipher referencing 'the founder's rest,' Dominic searches Halloway's mausoleum and finds a hidden stair — and fresh boot prints. Someone has been living below. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: dread and awe; the past is not merely remembered, it is inhabited.

chapters.title: The Old Man in the Dark
chapters.summary: In the crypt, Dominic finds Edmund Halloway himself — ninety-one, half-blind, hiding for thirty years while Vane's payments kept him buried in name. Halloway confesses everything but refuses to surface. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: compassion for a ghost who chose to become one.

chapters.title: Vane's Gambit
chapters.summary: Vane, tipped off, abducts Halloway from the crypt and frames Charles for the empty coffin. The town turns on the heirs; Brandt declares the case closed. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: fury and helplessness as the truth is weaponized.

chapters.title: What Iris Carried
chapters.summary: Iris discovers Brandt has been on Vane's retainer since the eighties — the 'accidents' Dominic solved were Vane's cleanups, and Brandt knew. She photographs the proof and sends a copy to Dominic, then disappears. POV: Iris. Emotional beat: courage sharpened by fear into resolve.

chapters.title: The Decoded Inheritance
chapters.summary: Working from memory, Dominic reconstructs the ledger: the fortune was never Halloway's alone — it was the town's, stolen and laundered through the founding families, Vane as architect. The inheritance theme turns literal. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: grim clarity; the town's beloved history is a crime scene.

chapters.title: Trade at the Mill
chapters.summary: Vane contacts Dominic: Halloway for the ledger, midnight at the derelict mill. Dominic agrees, hiding Iris's evidence as insurance, knowing Vane intends no witnesses. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: cold calm before sacrifice; an old detective spending himself as currency.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Iris, freed from a locked records room, races to the mill against orders. Dominic stalls Vane as Halloway collapses; Brandt arrives to bury the scene. Iris's arrival with state police tips the balance — she arrests Brandt herself. POV: Iris. Emotional beat: climax of the heart; duty and love finally pointing the same direction.

chapters.title: Confession and Currency
chapters.summary: Cornered, Vane bargains; Dominic trades the reconstructed ledger for a full recorded confession, sparing Charles and Margaret. Halloway, dying, asks to be carried home. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: bittersweet victory; justice bought with the truth's only price.

chapters.title: A Proper Burial
chapters.summary: Edmund Halloway is buried at last, in truth, before the whole town. Margaret endows the bookshop with the recovered fortune; Dominic refuses a detective's badge but accepts belonging. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into homecoming.

chapters.title: The Shop on Amberdale Lane
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the bookshop reopens — 'Amberdale & Vale.' Iris keeps her badge and her shelf by the window. A stranger leaves a coded note on the counter: another accident, another town, another ledger. POV: Iris. Emotional beat: quiet joy shadowed by a door left deliberately open.

chapters.title: Two Ledgers
chapters.summary: Dominic and Iris examine the stranger's cipher together over closing coffee, choosing the case — and each other — with open eyes. The final image: two ledgers on the counter, one for the town it shows, one for the truth it buries. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: resolution as beginning; belonging found, and a promise kept.
